doc.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001

title: Anonymous rock and roll dates
summary: Raph describes playing on many rock and roll dates without knowing whose they were, including Blood, Sweat & Tears and Bob Dylan.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: You mentioned doing rock & roll date.
Did you even know the name of the bands that you were playing for sometimes?
So you just came in, like a horn section, and they’d put the music in front of you, and you’d put the headphones on—
I did stuff for Blood, Sweat & Tears, I did stuff for Bob Dylan. Who’s the guy with the raindrops? Not Burt Bacharach, the other guy.
Not that one the other guy.

I can’t think of his name. Anyway, I’ll think of his name later, after I leave here. But a lot of the various people. I did a lot of work for them. I never knew who it was going to be. And occasionally somebody would tell me you remember the date we did for so-and-so? Well they’re playing it a lot. And I’d say oh did I do that? Was I on that? It just never really — I would keep an account of the jazz dates that I did, or the symphonic dates, because they to me were a little more meaningful. But some of these others, where you just sit down and play a few figures and it didn’t really matter who you were playing for or what you were playing for, you just did your job and did it as well as you could.
Most likely you’d get one or two passes at those things and they’d be done, right?
